newsitem.title: USA: Calif senator urges FTC to bar Shell-Texaco merger.
newsitem.headline: Calif senator urges FTC to bar Shell-Texaco merger.

text.p: U.S. Senator Barbara Boxer Thursday urged the Federal Trade Commission to reject the proposed merger of Shell Oil Co and Texaco Inc's western refining and marketing operations.

"This merger is bad for competition, bad for consumers, and bad for small business," the California Democrat said at a press conference, where she released a letter she was sending to FTC chairman Robert Pitofsky.
Boxer was backed by four consumer groups, which are all concerned that the merger will drive gasoline prices higher on the West Coast.
"I am writing to urge you to block the proposed merger between Shell oil and Texaco, Inc.," Boxer said in her June 19 letter to the FTC.
"If allowed to proceed, this merger would further decrease oil industry competition in California and result in higher gas prices for California consumers," the letter said.

"Today, California consumers regularly spend 10-30 cents more per gallon of gasoline than do drivers in other states. There is no market-based explanation for this clear gouging of California consumers," Boxer wrote.

Consumer group Citizen Action and Consumer Federation of America recently wrote to the FTC making the same arguments against the proposed merger, which they said would result in four oil giants controlling 80 percent of the West Coast retail gasoline market.

Boxer, a longtime consumer advocate, said the California refiners could get away with charging higher prices because competition was limited, and not because they had to sell much cleaner gasoline in California than anywhere else.
"(California prices are) so much higher that you can't possibly explain it away on the cleaner fuel," Boxer said.

Citizen Action's energy policy director Edwin Rothschild said that given the FTC's recent decision to block the Staples-Office Depot merger proposal, the agency had to reject the Shell-Texaco plan. "This one's a no-brainer," he said.
Boxer was hailed Wednesday night by the Consumer Federation of America with an award for championing consumer issues over the last decade.

While she wrote to the FTC alone, she said she was going to ask other western lawmakers to support her effort to raise concern about the Shell-Texaco proposal. "We'll follow it aggressively at the FTC," she said.
